newsitem.title: CANADA: Molson sells Novamax unit to Germany's Henkel.
newsitem.headline: Molson sells Novamax unit to Germany's Henkel.

text.p: Canadian brewing giant Molson Cos. Ltd. agreed to sell its Novamax Technologies unit to Germany's Henkel KGaA on Thursday, ending a troubled foray into speciality chemicals as Molson returns to its 210-year-old brewing roots.
The C$255 million ($187 million) sale of Atlanta-based Novamax completes Molson's sale of its Diversey chemical units, which had been a drag on the company's earnings in recent years.
The Diversey selloff added over C$1.2 billion ($882 million) to Molson's coffers as the company scours the world for a deal to expand its core brewing operations.

"We're pleased with the result of this final stage of the divestment of the Diversey group of companies," Brian Crombie, Molson's senior-vice president of corporate finance, said in a telephone interview.
Molson said it will sign a definitive deal with Henkel, a chemicals and consumer products group based in Dusseldorf, on or before Oct. 9.
Henkel said in a separate statement Novamax will boost its worldwide metallochemistry business in the United States, Europe, Asia and South America.
Novamax reported sales of C$284 million ($208 million) for the year ended March 31, 1996.
Analysts said Molson did better than expected on the Novamax sale.
"It's a good price. Originally, estimates were somewhere around C$200 million ($147 million)," said Bill Chisholm, an analyst with Deacon Capital Corp.
Earlier this year, Molson sold most of Diversey's worldwide cleaning and sanitizing businesses to British/Dutch giant Unilever Plc for C$780 million ($573 million).
It also sold Diversey's money-losing U.S. institutional and commercial laundry business to a management-led group.
In May, Illinois-based Nalco Chemical Co. picked up Diversey Water Technologies for C$112 million ($82 million).
Molson is seeking a buyer for its retail assets, which include stakes in Home Depot Inc.'s Canadian unit and home improvement chain Groupe Val Royal Inc. Molson also owns Beaver Lumber Co.
The Toronto-based company will be left with a 40 percent stake in Molson Breweries, Canada's biggest brewer, which makes Molson Canadian, Golden and Red Dog.
It also owns the famed Montreal Canadiens of the National Hockey League and the Molson Centre in which the club plays.
Molson's class A stock was up 25 cents Canadian (18 cents) to C$19.65 ($14.45) on the Toronto Stock Exchange, but remained well below its 52-week high of C$25.125 ($18.47).
